Smoke instruments from plume data

Source: R/apx2.R
smkiv.Rd

Builds the wildfire-smoke instruments of the recent papers from a daily smoke-plume record by place: the presence of a plume; the presence adjusted to the plumes that reached the ground; plume density classes; smoke-attributable fine particles; and counts by month.

Usage

smkiv(
  data,
  plume,
  unit,
  day,
  pm = NULL,
  adj = c("raw", "own", "nbr"),
  nbr = NULL,
  z = 1.64,
  seas = NULL,
  dens = NULL,
  cf = c("mean", "median", "childs"),
  by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per place and day.

plume

The name of the plume column (0 or 1).

unit, day

The names of the place and day columns.

pm

NULL or the name of the PM2.5 column (needed for "own", "nbr" and spm).

adj

"raw", "own" or "nbr".

nbr

For "nbr", the name of the column naming each row's nearest neighbouring place (a value of unit).

z

The number of standard deviations above the background.

seas

NULL (meteorological seasons of a date day) or the name of a season column.

dens

NULL or the name of a density-class column (NA or "" for no plume).

cf

"mean", "median" or "childs": the background of spm.

by

NULL or the name of a grouping column (place-month) to aggregate to.

Value

A data frame, one row per row of data (or per by group): smoke (0 or 1, or the count of smoke days per group), bg (the background, with pm), spm (with pm), and one indicator (or count) per density class, dens:<class>.

Details

The choices and their sources:

  • adj = "raw": the plume indicator as given. Kircheis (2026, p. 4) instruments daily PM2.5 by "a daily binary indicator of predicted ground-level wildfire smoke presence" from a machine-learning product; Lee and Lee (2026, p. 6) use the same smoke days and, as a robustness check, NOAA's Hazard Mapping System plumes alone.

  • adj = "own": a plume day counts only when the place's PM2.5 is more than z standard deviations above its background, the mean of its days without a plume in the same season (Burkhardt et al. 2019, footnote 13: the own-county adjusted variable, 1.64 standard deviations, the 95th percentile under normality).

  • adj = "nbr": the same test made with the plume and the PM2.5 of the nearest neighbouring place (nbr), Burkhardt et al.'s preferred neighbour-adjusted variable (p. 11-12), which avoids using the place's own PM2.5 in its instrument.

  • seas: the season of the background. Burkhardt et al. say "three month seasonal mean" without naming the months; the default is the meteorological seasons (December to February, ...) from a date column, pooled over years; give your own column to choose otherwise.

  • dens: density classes (HMS "light", "medium", "heavy") become one indicator each. Lee and Lee (2026, footnote 4) warn that HMS density before 2018 has large measurement error, and use presence only.

  • spm: smoke-attributable PM2.5, PM2.5 less the place-season background (cf = "mean", Burkhardt et al.'s background, or "median"), on adjusted smoke days and at least 0; 0 on other days. This counterfactual is crimlab's construction from Burkhardt et al.'s background. cf = "childs" is instead the definition of Childs et al. (2022, equations 1-3, p. 13609): the background is the median PM2.5 of the same place and calendar month over the year and the years either side (three years) on days without smoke (plume 0), and smoke PM2.5 is PM2.5 above it on smoke days (plume 1), at least 0, and 0 on other days; a place-month-year with no smoke-free days in its window gets NA, with a warning. It needs day as dates and ignores seas and adj (their smoke days are the plume column as given). Their machine-learned gridded smoke PM2.5 is a data product to be supplied as a column, not rebuilt here.

  • by: with a group (place and month), the counts of smoke days and the means of the rest per group, Burkhardt et al.'s county-month instrument, "the number of days a county is affected by a fire smoke plume in a given month" (p. 10).

Bao and Da (2026, sec. 3.3) keep only "Medium and Heavy plumes" because "including Light plumes badly overstates surface-smoke days" (give the density classes in dens and use their indicators), and instead of a plume overhead count the days a county lies downwind of a plume (dwnexp()).

The instrument must move the exposure (a first stage, see ivfe()) and change the outcome only through it: smoke may also keep people indoors or darken the day (Lee and Lee 2026 discuss both), which the exclusion restriction rules out by assumption.

References

Childs, M. L., Li, J., Wen, J., Heft-Neal, S., Driscoll, A., Wang, S., Gould, C. F., Qiu, M., Burney, J. and Burke, M. (2022). Daily local-level estimates of ambient wildfire smoke PM2.5 for the contiguous US. Environmental Science and Technology, 56(19), 13607-13621. doi:10.1021/acs.est.2c02934

Burkhardt, J., Bayham, J., Wilson, A., Berman, J. D., O'Dell, K., Ford, B., Fischer, E. V. and Pierce, J. R. (2019). The relationship between monthly air pollution and violent crime across the United States. Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy, 9(2), 188-205. doi:10.1080/21606544.2019.1630014

Kircheis, L. (2026). Wildfire smoke increases assaults: evidence from Seattle. Environmental Research Letters, 21, 044020. doi:10.1088/1748-9326/ae436c

Lee, G. and Lee, S. (2026). The impact of wildfire smoke exposure on crime. Environmental and Resource Economics, 89, 5. doi:10.1007/s10640-025-01053-2

Bao, J. and Da, Y. (2026). Wildfire smoke and crime: evidence from California. Working paper, Renmin University of China.

See also

ppmlcf(), exprun(), dwnexp()

Examples

# simulated plumes and PM2.5 in two places over 120 days
set.seed(6)
d <- data.frame(place = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 120),
                day = rep(as.Date("2024-06-01") + 0:119, 2))
d$plume <- rbinom(240, 1, 0.2)
d$pm <- rnorm(240, 8, 2) + d$plume * rbinom(240, 1, 0.5) * 15
d$near <- ifelse(d$place == "a", "b", "a")
s <- smkiv(d, "plume", "place", "day", pm = "pm", adj = "own")
table(raw = d$plume, adjusted = s$smoke)
#>    adjusted
#> raw   0   1
#>   0 186   0
#>   1  25  29
head(smkiv(d, "plume", "place", "day", pm = "pm", adj = "nbr", nbr = "near"))
#>   smoke       bg spm
#> 1     0 7.978119   0
#> 2     0 7.978119   0
#> 3     0 7.978119   0
#> 4     0 7.978119   0
#> 5     0 7.978119   0
#> 6     0 7.978119   0
